fields.meta_title: Credit Application Form Builder for Businesses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A credit application form that emails trade references, routes large requests to a credit manager and saves every account to your own database.
fields.h1: Build a Credit Application Form for New Trade Accounts
fields.hero_description: A credit application form tells a supplier who a new customer is and how they pay other suppliers. Describe your terms, and Emergent builds the form and an accounts table.
fields.features_heading: What a Business Credit File Holds
fields.features_subheading: A Word template comes back scanned, with phone numbers to chase. These six features turn it into a file you can decide on.
fields.feature_1:
The questions a credit manager asks

Asks for the legal name and EIN, then years in business, the amount requested and trade and bank references. Required fields stop a file from arriving with the bank reference blank.
fields.feature_2:
An email to every trade reference

Emails each reference two questions: the highest credit it extends and how fast the applicant pays. Replies land on the applicant's row, and silence for three days gets a reminder.
fields.feature_3:
Uploads read into fields

Reads uploaded resale certificates and financial statements into fields like certificate number and annual revenue. A field read with low confidence goes to a person to confirm.
fields.feature_4:
Guarantee and terms signed on screen

Captures the owner's signature on your terms of sale and any personal guarantee. The file stores the signer's name, the time they signed and the version of the terms they saw.
fields.feature_5:
Routing set by the amount requested

Sends small requests to an analyst and large ones to the credit manager. A Slack alert flags each new file, and every approved amount is logged with who approved it and when.
fields.feature_6:
Source code in your GitHub repo

Exports the full app to your GitHub repo. A developer can connect it to your ERP or accounting system through its API, or you can describe any change in a prompt instead.

fields.usecase_heading: Credit Applications by Type of Supplier
fields.tab_content_1:
References answer by email before the first order

Harbor Foods Supply opens restaurant accounts on net 30 terms. Each owner lists three suppliers the restaurant buys from, and each one gets an email asking what limit it allows and whether the restaurant pays on time. Juniper Bistro has two of three replies in, and the third gets a reminder after three days.
fields.tab_content_2:
Requests over $25,000 go to the credit manager

Cobalt Packaging's credit policy has one line: any request over $25,000 needs two years of financial statements and the credit manager's review. Smaller requests go to an analyst. When Pinecrest Foods asks for $40,000, the form will not submit without both statements, and the file reaches the credit manager in Slack.
fields.tab_content_3:
Resale certificates read into the account record

Contractors opening an account at Granite Ridge Building Supply attach a resale certificate. The form reads the certificate number and expiration date onto the account. On the Bellmont Builders file, the date came back with low confidence, and a clerk checks it against the scan before the account opens.
fields.tab_content_4:
The owner signs before any equipment leaves

Summit Equipment Rental will not send a skid steer out on account until the paperwork is done. New customers apply on a phone at the counter, and the last screen shows the personal guarantee in full for the owner to sign with a finger. Dario Vance signed at 7:40 AM, and his file went to credit review complete.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Credit Application Form
fields.howto_description: Write the credit policy before the form. Every question and every decision letter follows from it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep protected traits off the form
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set your standard terms, such as net 30, and the limit at which a request moves to a senior reviewer. Decide what each tier requires: trade references below that line, financial statements above it. Each question on the form should trace back to the policy.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act bars credit decisions based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age or receipt of public assistance. For individual unsecured credit, Regulation B also bars asking about marital status outside community property states.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for trade references from suppliers who sell to the applicant on terms, plus a bank reference. Get an email address for each contact, not only a phone number. A supplier the applicant pays in advance has no payment record to report.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give Emergent the policy as written, plus the uploads you need from applicants, such as financial statements or a resale certificate. It builds the application and a database table for the accounts. Changing a question later takes one more prompt.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add the terms and the guarantee
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put your terms of sale on the final screen, with the personal guarantee if your policy calls for one and a line allowing you to contact the listed references. The signer types or draws a signature, and the app keeps a copy of the exact terms shown to them.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the references, then set a limit
fields.howto_step_6_des: Check what each trade reference reported: the highest credit it extended and how late the applicant pays, if ever. Compare that with the amount requested. The credit manager records the approved limit and the reason for it on the account, where anyone reviewing it later can read it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Regulation B gives a creditor 30 days after a completed application to approve, counteroffer or deny it, and that clock covers businesses with revenue of $1 million or less. A denied applicant can request the specific reasons within 60 days.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable PDFs, Word templates and the CFPB model forms, all of which end at a signature line and leave a credit team re-keying the file and phoning references. This page shows what a business credit application asks for, the Regulation B rules on what to leave out and when to answer, then builds what a template cannot: trade references emailed from the form, limit-based routing, certificates read into fields, a guarantee signed on a phone and one table of every account.

claims_to_source: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act prohibits credit discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age or receipt of public assistance
Regulation B requires a creditor to notify an applicant of approval, counteroffer or adverse action within 30 days after receiving a completed application
A denied applicant is entitled to a statement of specific reasons if requested within 60 days
Regulation B notification rules apply to business credit, and for businesses with gross revenues of $1 million or less the creditor may give the adverse action statement orally
For individual unsecured credit, a creditor may not ask about marital status unless the applicant lives in a community property state or relies on property there

The sample denial notice in Regulation B (form C-1) lists credit application incomplete first, and includes insufficient number of credit references, unable to verify credit references, excessive obligations in relation to income and number of recent inquiries
Regulation B includes model credit application forms (Appendix B) that creditors may use
